title: Ada and the Hollow
premise: Ada Orsen Crane, gatekeeper of the sealed Thornfell pass, inherits a dying stranger's map — a chart of the Hollow, the buried city where an ancient war was truly won and its victors' names erased. Hunted by the Ashen Order, who want the map burned, and shadowed by a smuggler whose loyalty she cannot price, Ada discovers the stranger was her own mother, long believed dead. The map leads not to treasure but to the Hollow's memory-vaults, where the truth of the war could either free the mountain clans or hand the Order a weapon. In the end Ada must choose between destroying the vault and letting the world remember: she opens it, at the cost of the smuggler's life and her own place as keeper, and walks out of the mountains carrying a history no one asked her to hold.
about_author: C. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing contested histories in border towns before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who inherit other people's secrets.

chapters.title: The Gate That Stays Shut
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Establishes her solitary life tending the Thornfell gate, her rituals of inspection, and her wary friendship with the smuggler Bren who trades below the pass. A storm breaks; emotional beat: comfortable loneliness about to be shattered.

chapters.title: A Stranger in the Snow
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She finds a dying woman on the smugglers' road who presses a leather-wrapped map into her hands and whispers 'you already know why.' The woman dies before saying more. Beat: dread and unwanted inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The map depicts the Hollow, a city Ada knows only from forbidden lullabies. Bren notices her distraction and lies badly about not recognizing it. Beat: first crack in trust.

chapters.title: Grey Cloaks at the Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Agents of the Ashen Order arrive asking after a dead woman. Ada lies for the first time in her careful life and realizes how easily she can. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Bren's Price
chapters.summary: Bren's POV. He reveals he was hired weeks ago to watch for the map's courier — by someone he never met. He chooses to warn Ada instead of reporting her. Beat: loyalty chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Down the Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The two flee through Bren's secret paths while Order riders sweep the passes. Ada learns the mountains' hidden grammar from him. Beat: reluctant partnership becoming something warmer.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They shelter in a clan village where no one remembers the war, only that remembering is unlucky. An elder recognizes the map's seal and goes pale. Beat: memory as wound.

chapters.title: Lullabies With Teeth
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The elder tells the children's rhymes Ada half-remembers — and one verse describes the dying stranger's face. Ada begins to suspect who the woman was. Beat: grief arriving ahead of proof.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Split Stone
chapters.summary: Bren's POV. An Order patrol corners them; Bren takes a knife meant for Ada and kills for the first time in years. They escape but he is wounded. Beat: the cost of choosing a side.

chapters.title: Fever Promises
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Tending Bren's fever, she confesses the whole truth to his unconscious form — then finds him awake at the end of it. Beat: intimacy forced by honesty.

chapters.title: The Order's Offer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. An Order commander catches up alone and offers Ada her old life back if she surrenders the map, revealing the Order burns it because the vault would vindicate the losing side. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: What Mother Left
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hidden stitching inside the map's backing yields a letter: the stranger was Ada's mother, alive all these years, guarding the map until Ada was ready. Beat: fury and love colliding.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Trail
chapters.summary: Bren's POV. Evidence suggests someone in the clan villages sold their route to the Order. Bren suspects himself — his old debts make him plausible. Beat: self-doubt corroding loyalty.

chapters.title: Into the Underfell
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They descend beneath the mountains through flooded mine-shafts toward the Hollow, pursued by the traitor's tipped-off hunters. Beat: commitment past the point of return.

chapters.title: Doors That Remember Hands
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The Hollow's gates open to her bloodline — her mother's key written in her skin. The dead city lights around them. Beat: awe and belonging she never expected.

chapters.title: The Memory-Vaults
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Inside the vaults, recorded memories replay the war's true ending: the victors didn't win, they erased. Among the records, her mother's own testimony waits. Beat: truth as burden.

chapters.title: The Face Behind the Grey
chapters.summary: Bren's POV. The commander enters the vaults with the traitor revealed — the forgetful village's elder, who sold them to spare his people reprisal. Battle breaks out among the shelves of memory. Beat: betrayal with comprehensible motives.

chapters.title: Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Order tries to burn the vaults; Bren holds the door and is mortally wounded buying Ada time to reach the master record. Beat: sacrifice as the final proof of found family.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Voice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her mother's recorded testimony asks Ada to decide what the world deserves: comfort or truth. The commander begs her to destroy it. Beat: the thematic choice distilled.

chapters.title: Opening the Hollow
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She releases the memories to every mind connected to the mountain — the clans remember, the Order's lie collapses, and the commander kneels in the ruins of his certainty. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Bren's Last Road
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Bren dies in the lit Hollow, asking to be remembered by name — which, now, everyone is. Ada buries him where the gate can see. Beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Walked Out
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada leaves the gate unsealed and descends to the changed lowlands, carrying her mother's letter and Bren's name into a world that finally remembers. Beat: bittersweet resolution — truth costs everything and is still worth it.
